description: SAME AS clause in a data description entry — the subject takes the SAME description as data-name-1's entry, subordinates included (ISO §2023:13.18.49.4 GR1/GR2; levels renumber relative to the subject). A COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 data description entry's Format 1 offers data-name-1/FILLER, REDEFINES, PICTURE, USAGE, SIGN, OCCURS, SYNCHRONIZED, JUSTIFIED, BLANK WHEN ZERO and VALUE, and no SAME AS clause (§1985:VI.5.3.3 SR2: 'The remaining clauses may be written in any order'), and AS is no 1985 reserved word (§1985:IV.8 runs AREAS, ASCENDING: its rows '| AREAS | DE | EOP | JUSTIFIED |' and '| ASCENDING | DEBUG-CONTENTS | EQUAL | |'); §2002:13.16.47 reads 'The SAME AS clause specifies that a data-name has the same description as that specified by another data description entry' (§2002:13.16.47.3 GR1: 'The effect of the SAME AS clause is as though the data description identified by data-name-1 had been coded in place of the SAME AS clause'), §2002:F.1 item 6 adds AS to the reserved words, and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 117: 'The SAME AS clause indicates that the description of a data item is identical to that of another item.' §2014:13.18.49 and §2014:13.18.49.3 GR1 carry the 2002 text, so 2014 = 2023. LIVE (P10 Step 16): expansion rides the ONE ExpandTypes/CloneItem machinery (ExpandSameAs); §2023:13.16.3 SR12 composition + the §2023:13.18.49.3 SRs enforce as COBOL1555/1556/1557.
vcr: 2002 introduction (§2002:13.16.47; §2002:F.2 item 117; the TYPEDEF/SAME AS data-description family)
